source.title: Phonological Abstraction and Exception Memorization in Noisy Tone Learning
source.authors: Yi Yang; Yi-Ming Wang; Jia-Hong Yuan

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test performance across model-depth interventions, training-data scales, and epochs, but it does not reproduce the original double-descent method or identify an interpolation threshold.
record.gate_note: The paper cites double descent in its background, but those citations are not its results. The rows below cover its own size, data-scale, and epoch-wise test-accuracy results. Perturbation probes and abstraction/memorization measures are not rows because they do not measure the claimed double-descent behavior.
record.test_reason: The study is not aimed at double descent; it cites Nakkiran et al. only in background. Its own results still bear on parts of V2 and V3 in a new setting: wav2vec2.0 and HuBERT fine-tuned on Mandarin tone classification with label noise. It reports test accuracy over epochs, at models that reach 100% training accuracy, and across a 7×10 grid of training scale × label noise. The authors never analyse these results as double descent. All numbers are single runs, and the grid uses early-stopped (best-validation) checkpoints. T3 fits better than T2 because the method is not aimed at the double-descent question.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that in recoverable noise regimes the model first learns abstraction-consistent tone behaviour and only later memorizes corrupted labels. Late fitting is benign at low noise, sharply degrades generalization near the noise boundary, and at 90% noise no abstraction is recovered. The pattern persists under truncated encoders, and rank compression is not selective. Fitted exceptions are fragile under acoustic perturbation. They draw no conclusion about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses noisy-label tone classification, data-scale and encoder-capacity interventions, and epoch-wise behavioral probes; it does not reproduce the original double-descent experiments or locate interpolation thresholds.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported learning trajectory and data-scale effects vary with label-noise ratio and training scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the acoustic rank bottleneck at 80% noise, higher rank gives lower best-validation accuracy: 46.6 at r=2 vs 36.4 at r=64. At 50–70% noise, higher rank helps (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near a label-noise recoverability boundary, added representational capacity can lower test accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026
record.problems: Reported numbers are single-run percentages, with no uncertainty estimates. The model-size comparison uses only selected encoder depths, and the study does not locate an interpolation threshold. Epoch-wise evidence is summarized for representative settings rather than reported as a full numerical curve for each configuration.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining Figure 1 scale-noise grid cells and supplementary scale/noise configurations are omitted; representative cells relevant to data-scale changes are retained in r5–r9. Capacity rank-intervention and acoustic-perturbation results are omitted because they do not directly measure model-size double descent, epoch-wise test-error double descent, or an interpolation-threshold data effect.

untested.parts: No dense size sweep crosses the interpolation threshold; every depth reaches 100% training accuracy. Reported accuracies are early-stopped, so model-wise double descent cannot be read.
No long training beyond interpolation that could reveal a second descent. Training runs for roughly 15–29 epochs.
No interpolation threshold is located and no seeds or uncertainty are reported. Results use early-stopped checkpoints rather than end-of-training test error.
Not framed or tested. The noise dependence of the epoch-wise rise (r10 vs r11) is suggestive but is not about a double-descent peak or about regularization.

missing.what: Last-epoch vs best-validation test accuracy per depth: for example 12L 56.6 vs 88.2, and 2L at 90% noise 25.8 vs 22.2. This gives epoch-wise degradation without recovery across model sizes.
Post-encoder rank ablation: best test 83.4–89.7 falls to final test 49.6–55.7 once training accuracy reaches 99.5–99.9%.
HuBERT epoch-wise trajectories at 10% scale across noise levels 0–90%.
Non-monotonic accuracy in scale at 90% noise (27.2, 24.5, 22.2, 29.8, 25.7, 19.6, 20.5); near chance and single runs.

record.verdict_notes: Relation is borderline. Double descent is only cited in background, and the bearing results are incidental single-run numbers that the authors never analyse as double descent. Rows r5 and r7 are baseline cells rather than results. The V1 rows cannot show model-wise double descent because values are early-stopped and every depth interpolates. The epoch-wise rise without recovery may reflect the short training budget rather than the absence of a second descent.

versions.untested_parts: The depth comparison does not trace a dense model-size sweep or locate a size at which training data are just fit.
The paper reports selected trajectories and representative extrema, not a test-error fall-rise-fall curve over a complete training run.
The study varies training-data scale and measures test accuracy, but does not locate an interpolation threshold or establish that its high-noise settings are near one.

relationships.condition: Label noise of 50–70%: pretrained wav2vec2.0 large at 5% scale, and randomly initialized wav2vec2.0 at 100% scale. Training budget roughly 15–20 epochs.
relationships.reason: Test error falls, then rises sharply after an early peak, but no second descent appears even after the models reach about 100% training accuracy (r11, r13). The text adds similar best-to-last drops for Table 1, Table 8 and HuBERT (Figure 4).
relationships.display_finding: At 50–70% label noise, test error fell then rose sharply without a second descent within roughly 15–20 epochs, despite training accuracy reaching about 100%.

source_check.condition: Label noise of 50–70%: pretrained wav2vec2.0 large at 5% scale, and randomly initialized wav2vec2.0 at 100% scale. Training budget roughly 15–20 epochs.
source_check.reason: r11 and r13 show early improvement followed by substantial deterioration; Table 10 shows only a small subsequent recovery. This is incomplete V2 behavior within the observed windows. Near-perfect exception memorization should not be equated with a reported total-training-accuracy measurement for these runs.

relationships.condition: Low label noise (10%), wav2vec2.0 large at 5% scale
relationships.reason: There is no epoch-wise rise in test error at all: 90.1 at peak vs 88.3 at the final epoch (r10).

relation.reason: Its own test-accuracy trajectories and controlled training-scale comparisons bear on the claim versions, despite double descent appearing only in the background discussion.

tranche.reason: The study investigates phonological learning in a new speech-classification setting, with its own epoch-wise and data-scale results bearing on V2 and V3.

source_check.notes: Noise percentages denote nominal label replacement, not realized changed-label rates. Best-validation grid values differ from peak test accuracy; exception memorization is distinct from total training accuracy.

statements.correction: Figure 2: pretrained wav2vec2.0 large, 5% scale, 70% noise, approximately 15 epochs; 10% noise, approximately 18 epochs. Table 10: random initialization, 100% scale, 50% noise, reported through epoch 20. Figure 4: HuBERT, 10% scale, plots through epoch 29.
statements.problem: The qualitative trajectory description is accurate, but the named runs end at approximately 15, 18 and 20 epochs. The 29-epoch plots concern HuBERT at 10% scale.
